subject: science
passage: Many cat owners believe that a purring cat is always a happy cat. Cats often purr while being stroked or while resting in a warm lap, so it seems natural to treat the sound as a sign of contentment.
passage_b: Veterinarians report that cats also purr in situations that are anything but pleasant, such as when they are injured, giving birth, or close to death. According to animal behaviorist Ingrid Solberg, purring may sometimes help a cat calm itself during stress rather than simply express pleasure.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the belief in Text 1?

choices.A: By noting that cats also purr when they are hurt or under stress
choices.B: By arguing that cats purr only when they are in pain or afraid
choices.C: By claiming that cats purr most often when they are being stroked
choices.D: By agreeing that purring is a reliable sign that a cat is content

explanation.why: Text 1 describes the belief that "a purring cat is always a happy cat." Text 2 reports that cats also purr when they are "injured, giving birth, or close to death" and that purring may help a cat "calm itself during stress." So the author of Text 2 would point out that purring does not always mean contentment.
explanation.A: Correct. Text 2 lists painful and stressful situations in which cats purr, which challenges the idea that purring always means a cat is happy.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says purring may "sometimes" help a cat calm itself; it does not say cats purr only when in pain.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 never compares how often cats purr in different situations.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 gives examples of cats purring in unpleasant situations, so its author would not call purring a reliable sign of contentment.
